# LedgerLocal

> LedgerLocal is a browser-based bank statement converter that turns PDF bank statements, scanned documents, and photos into Excel, CSV, and other accounting formats — entirely on-device, with no file ever uploaded to a server.

Bank detection: named parsing for 23+ banks across the US, UK, Canada, and India, plus a generic layout parser for any other bank's text-based PDF statement.

Export formats: Excel (.xlsx), CSV, Tally XML, OFX, QIF, QBO, and IIF (QuickBooks Desktop).

Pricing: 6 pages per PDF with no signup required (unlimited separate conversions); a 10-page lifetime allowance (PDF pages and photo/scan conversions combined) once signed up for a free account; unlimited pages and conversions on the paid Pro plan. Structured-file conversions (CSV, IIF, OFX, QFX, QIF, MT940 — see below) do not count against any limit, since they don't require OCR.

Privacy architecture: PDF text extraction, OCR (for scanned pages or photos), and all format conversion run client-side in the browser (pdf.js, tesseract.js) — there is no server-side processing step and no file is ever transmitted. Transaction categorisation also runs on-device, using a deterministic rules engine rather than a model, so the same description always yields the same category and nothing is sent anywhere to work it out.

Output columns: Date, Payee, Description, Category, Transaction ID, Amount, Dr/Cr and Balance, plus Account for files containing more than one statement. Payee and Category are derived on-device from the bank's own description text; the raw description is always preserved alongside them, never replaced.

Accuracy handling: LedgerLocal publishes no single accuracy percentage, on the grounds that one figure across every bank worldwide is not a meaningful claim. Instead every row carries a confidence score (0-99, never 100), rows below the threshold are flagged for review before export, and each running balance is reconciled against the previous row so arithmetic breaks surface rather than passing silently.

Locale handling: the decimal separator is inferred once per document from the statement's own contents, so comma-decimal formats (1.234,56) and zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW, VND, IDR) parse correctly alongside dot-decimal ones. Dates cover ISO, slash, dash, dot-separated (03.04.2025) and year-first (2025/04/03) forms, with day/month order inferred per document. Column headers are recognised in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Portuguese. Named bank support remains US, UK, Canada and India; the above widens what can be read, not what has been tested.

## File format converters (no bank statement PDF required)

- [CSV to IIF](https://ledgerlocal.com/csv-to-iif) / [IIF to CSV](https://ledgerlocal.com/iif-to-csv)
- [CSV to QIF](https://ledgerlocal.com/csv-to-qif) / [QIF to CSV](https://ledgerlocal.com/qif-to-csv)
- [CSV to OFX](https://ledgerlocal.com/csv-to-ofx) / [OFX to CSV](https://ledgerlocal.com/ofx-to-csv)
- [QFX to CSV](https://ledgerlocal.com/qfx-to-csv): QFX and OFX are the same underlying format; LedgerLocal reads both.
- [MT940 to CSV](https://ledgerlocal.com/mt940-to-csv): Read direction only — LedgerLocal does not currently export to MT940.

## QuickBooks (QBO) converters

- [QBO to Excel](https://ledgerlocal.com/qbo-to-excel): Long-form guide plus converter. Covers why Excel cannot open a .qbo file, what the OFX structure contains, the manual rename-to-XML route and its limits, and troubleshooting for raw DTPOSTED dates, OFX sign conventions, FITID and multi-account files.
- [QFX to Excel](https://ledgerlocal.com/qfx-to-excel): Guide plus converter for Quicken Web Connect files.
- [OFX to Excel](https://ledgerlocal.com/ofx-to-excel): Guide plus converter for the bank-neutral Open Financial Exchange format.
- [QBO to CSV](https://ledgerlocal.com/qbo-to-csv): Opens a QuickBooks Web Connect file as a spreadsheet. Also accepts .ofx and .qfx, since all three share the same underlying structure.
- [CSV to QBO](https://ledgerlocal.com/csv-to-qbo): Produces a QBO file importable by QuickBooks Online and Desktop.
- [QFX to QBO](https://ledgerlocal.com/qfx-to-qbo) / [OFX to QBO](https://ledgerlocal.com/ofx-to-qbo) / [QIF to QBO](https://ledgerlocal.com/qif-to-qbo)

Multi-account handling: a single OFX/QBO download often bundles several statements (for example a current account and a credit card). Each transaction is tagged with its own account, and Excel exports place each account on a separate sheet rather than interleaving them. FITID is preserved as the Transaction ID column so QuickBooks can detect duplicates on re-import, and timezone suffixes such as [0:GMT] are stripped from dates.

## Comparisons with other tools

These pages describe competitors structurally (how they charge, where processing runs) rather than quoting their prices, because pricing in this category is widely misreported across third-party sources and goes stale quickly. Each page also states plainly where the competitor is the better choice.

- [DocuClipper alternative](https://ledgerlocal.com/docuclipper-alternative): Cloud, per-page metered processing versus on-device with no limit.
- [MoneyThumb alternative](https://ledgerlocal.com/moneythumb-alternative): A separate desktop product per output format versus one converter for all of them.
- [ProperSoft alternative](https://ledgerlocal.com/propersoft-alternative): A separate desktop app per conversion pair; their converters handle structured files rather than PDF statements.
- [StatementDesk alternative](https://ledgerlocal.com/statementdesk-alternative): Same entry price, but metered by transaction rows and processed in the cloud.
